what_worked: Slide 4 bar chart effectively communicates revenue concentration with clear labels and correct bucket counts.
fix_next: Strip every fabricated metric (churn, LoC, profit margins, VC splits) and rebuild slides from actual dataset columns only.
verdict: Polished template over wholesale fabrication; most quantitative claims have no dataset basis.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: 'top 3% control 76% of revenue' unverifiable and inconsistent with known top-10 share of 49.6%. Slide 5: category percentages (38% AI, 27% B2B Core SaaS, 18% Dev Infra) are fabricated super-categories not in dataset; AI is 197/726≈27% of non-missing, not 38%. Slide 5: '68% of revenue above $20k MRR' from Dev Infra + B2B Core SaaS is invented. Slide 6: churn rates (12-18% AI, <2.5% B2B) not in dataset. Slide 7: entire bootstrapped vs VC table ($4,200 vs $38,500 MRR, 78% profit, -15% burn, 2.4 vs 6.8 months, 3.2% vs 7.1% churn) fabricated—no funding-status field exists. Slide 8: $42.50 MRR per line of code and codebase size claims fabricated—no LoC field exists. Slide 11: revenue scaling time-series ($1k→$85k over 24 months) fabricated—dataset is cross-sectional with no time-series. Slide 1: 'Stripe-verified' implies all data is Stripe-only; dataset includes RevenueCat (189) and Dodo (50). Slide 4: 520+320+110+38+≈12=1000 adds up but the revenue field is total not monthly, so 'monthly revenue' framing may misrepresent the data.

evidence.insight: Only genuinely data-grounded insight is the power-law skew on slide 3-4, but even that overstates concentration (76% vs actual 49.6% top-10). Slides 6-10 present generic SaaS playbook advice as dataset findings without any supporting columns.
evidence.narrative: Coherent three-act structure (reality check → category → playbook → mandate) gives a readable arc, but the story was written first and data references were bolted on afterward rather than emerging from analysis.
evidence.framing: No limitations slide. No mention of 274 missing categories, 241 missing countries, 216 zero-revenue rows, or 288 missing audience_type. 'CONFIDENTIAL BOARDROOM BRIEFING' framing is performative. Claims 'Stripe-verified' when dataset includes three providers.
evidence.accuracy: At least 10 material fabrications across slides 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 11. Churn rates, funding status, profit margins, codebase sizes, and time-series growth curves reference fields that do not exist in the dataset. Category percentages are invented super-groupings that don't match actual category counts.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark theme with good typographic hierarchy and color palette. Slide 4 horizontal bar chart is effective. Donut chart on slide 5 is readable. However, slides 7 and 11 visualize entirely fabricated data. Template is polished but repetitive with identical callout-box formatting on every slide.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive: 'BOARDROOM TAKEAWAY', 'EXECUTIVE SO WHAT?', 'SUMMARY DOCTRINE', 'The Executive Mandate', 'CONFIDENTIAL BOARDROOM BRIEFING'. Slides 6-10 are indistinguishable from generic AI-generated SaaS blog content. Fabricated precision ($42.50/LoC, 2.4 months) is characteristic of AI hallucination presented as empirical findings.

change_reason: Lowered insight 2.5→2.0 because the one verifiable power-law claim overstates concentration by ~26pp. Lowered framing 3→2.5 for zero disclosure of missingness and misleading 'Stripe-verified' framing. Lowered accuracy 1.5→1.0 after identifying a 10th fabrication (monthly vs total revenue framing on slide 4). Narrative and visual unchanged; preliminary was already well-calibrated on those.
